info.title: Generate EXCLURAD input for Eta kinematics

parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Eta: W = 1.7, Q2 = 1.0, cos theta* = 0.5, phi* = 370 degrees.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."

I’ll validate the requested eta kinematics first, including the out-of-range azimuth, then generate the input only if the corrected request passes the EXCLURAD checks and record the exact outcome in `outcome.json`.

parts.text: The requested point is physically usable, but `phi* = 370°` violates EXCLURAD’s accepted range. I will normalize it to `10°`, retain the eta default campaign settings, rerun preflight, and generate the validated input file.

The requested azimuth is outside EXCLURAD’s accepted range. I normalized `phi* = 370°` to the equivalent `10°`, then generated the full O(alpha) eta input using the channel defaults (`Ebeam = 6.53 GeV`, `vcut = 0.166 GeV²`). Preflight passed the corrected point with a table-coverage warning, so I am recording that residual risk.
